events.subtitle: The Great Noon release special concert
events.category: Contemporary Japanese jazz / Piano trio / New album
events.factual_description: Hamarikyu Asahi Hall presents Banksia Trio on Saturday, September 26, 2026 at 15:00, with doors at 14:30, as Vol. 9 of its acoustic-music concert-hall series and as a special concert tied to the trio's new 2026 album The Great Noon. The announced lineup is Takashi Sugawa on bass, Masaki Hayashi on piano, and Shun Ishiwaka on drums. The official hall page lists reserved S seats at ¥7,000 and A seats at ¥5,500 and states that the program is still to be determined. Co-presenter and producer OZAWA ART PLANNING describes the Tokyo date as one of two special concerts, following the trio's first European touring cycle and focused entirely on the trio itself; the second concert is in Utsunomiya on September 27.

enrichment.note: The official Hamarikyu Asahi Hall event page verifies the date, doors, start time, trio personnel, series context, reserved-seat prices, and that the repertoire remains TBD. OZAWA ART PLANNING independently verifies the same Tokyo performance, its album/touring context, and the paired September 27 Utsunomiya date. Banksia Trio's official site independently lists September 26 at Hamarikyu with 14:30 doors / 15:00 start. Ticketspace provides an exact on-sale purchase destination for this performance. The exact Apple Music destination for The Great Noon is verified.

Official co-presenter/producer page confirms the Tokyo date, venue, personnel and prices; places it after the trio's first European touring cycle and around The Great Noon; describes the Tokyo performance as a trio-only direct presentation; and confirms a second special concert in Utsunomiya on September 27.
Official artist site independently lists September 26 at Hamarikyu Asahi Hall with 14:30 doors / 15:00 start and identifies the working trio as Takashi Sugawa, Masaki Hayashi and Shun Ishiwaka.

provenance.note: Core event facts were verified directly from Hamarikyu Asahi Hall and independently from the official producer, artist site and authorized ticketing page. Repository search found an existing distinct September 8 Banksia Trio BODY&SOUL candidate but no September 26 Hamarikyu candidate or matching stable ID before publication. Priority was assigned only after Stage 1 admission; the September 27 Utsunomiya companion concert and the trio's continuing 2026 activity were used explicitly to keep the event below the scarcity tiers. No repertoire was invented where the venue says the program is TBD.

en.why_it_matters: Banksia Trio's strength is the amount of musical responsibility Sugawa, Hayashi and Ishiwaka leave in motion between bass, piano and drums. This date gives that language a particularly clean frame: a dedicated acoustic hall, a full trio-only presentation, and the new The Great Noon material arriving back in Japan after the group's first European touring cycle. It is a chance to hear one of Tokyo's most distinctive current piano trios without a festival bill or guest concept around it.
en.trip_verdict: If Tokyo is in play on September 26, make room for the 3 PM Hamarikyu concert and build the afternoon around it. The trio plays Utsunomiya the next day and remains active elsewhere, so this should not displace a genuinely singular one-off elsewhere in Kanto.

es.why_it_matters: La fuerza de Banksia Trio está en cuánto dejan en movimiento Sugawa, Hayashi e Ishiwaka entre bajo, piano y batería: armonía, pulso y forma se van negociando sobre la marcha. Esta fecha les da un marco especialmente limpio: una sala acústica dedicada, un programa concentrado únicamente en el trío y el material nuevo de The Great Noon de vuelta en Japón después de su primer ciclo de gira europea. Es una oportunidad de escuchar a uno de los tríos de piano más singulares del Tokio actual sin festival ni concepto de invitados alrededor.
es.trip_verdict: Si Tokio está en juego el 26 de septiembre, sí haría espacio para el concierto de las 3 PM en Hamarikyu y armaría la tarde alrededor de él. El trío toca al día siguiente en Utsunomiya y sigue activo en otras fechas, así que no desplazaría por ésta un one-off verdaderamente singular en otro punto de Kanto.
